messages.content: Help me signal the end of an XML element with the qualified name `{namespaceURI='http://www.example.com', localPart='item', prefix='ex'}` and augmentation information `augmentations` in an XML processing application that uses namespaces?

function.name: XMLNamespaceBinder_endElement
function.description: Signals the end of an XML element, handling namespace-related processing if namespaces are enabled, or delegating to the document handler otherwise. Note that the provided function is in Java 8 SDK syntax.

element.description: The qualified name of the element that is ending. Use QName object, has a constructor that takes in three parameters, namespaceURI, localPart, prefix This parameter can be of any type of Java object in string representation.

augs.description: Augmentation information associated with the element. This parameter can be of any type of Java object in string representation.

message.reasoning:
We need to call the tool function XMLNamespaceBinder_endElement with appropriate arguments.

The "qualified name" should be represented as a QName object constructed from namespaceURI, localPart, prefix. But we just pass it as string? It says "Use QName object, has a constructor that takes in three parameters". So maybe we provide something like new QName("http://...", "item", "ex") but since it's string representation, perhaps we give JSON-like structure? In previous tasks I've seen they expect us to supply the fully formed QName string e.g., "{namespaceURI='...',localPart='...'}"? Actually earlier examples show passing element: "new javax.xml.namespace.QName('uri','local','prefix')" ?

But here instructions say: "This parameter can be of any type of Java object in string representation." So we could send `"javax.xml.namespace.QName{namespaceURI=http://...,localPart=item,prefix=ex}"`. Or simply use the format described: {namespaceURI='http://www.example.com', localPart='item', prefix='ex'}

Thus element param: "{namespaceURI='http://www.example.com', localPart='item', prefix='ex'}"

Augmentations: "augmentations".

Let's produce function call accordingly.
